title: Cables that fit the job
summary: Identify connections by purpose and capability.

passages.heading: The core idea
passages.markdown: Choose a cable by the signal and environment it must support, then confirm the connector. Twisted-pair Ethernet commonly uses an eight-position modular connector often called RJ45. Optical fiber carries light and uses connectors such as LC or SC. Fiber avoids electrical interference along the cable and can suit longer links, but the transceivers, fiber type, and connector must match. A connector that physically fits does not prove end-to-end compatibility.

passages.heading: In the real world
passages.markdown: HDMI and DisplayPort commonly carry digital display signals. VGA carries analog video and does not become digital just because a passive connector adapter changes the plug shape. SATA is used for internal storage data connections, with power supplied separately. USB-C can support several functions, but only those implemented by the devices and cable. In installation spaces, cable jacket ratings also matter: use the appropriate rated cable for the building environment and follow applicable installation requirements rather than choosing purely by color or price.

passages.heading: Make it stick
passages.markdown: Put it into practice by explaining the decision in your own words. In a support scenario, identify the requirement first, connect it to the relevant technology, and check the result against that requirement. If the evidence changes, revisit your reasoning rather than repeating the same action. Document what you observed so the next person can understand your conclusion.
